thesis.what_must_be_true: Wolfspeed must convert its post-Chapter 11 balance-sheet reset (~$145M annualized cash interest, maturities in 2030/2031) into time for the 200mm ramp: Mohawk Valley device loadings and Siler City materials utilization must rise on AI datacenter, industrial/energy and eventually 800V auto demand so that underutilization costs shrink, gross margin crosses breakeven during FY2027, and operating cash burn narrows toward breakeven before the roughly $1.1B liquidity buffer (plus incentive refunds) is exhausted. If revenue stays near ~$150M/quarter with gross margins deeply negative, the cash runway forces another dilutive raise by FY2028.

validated.preview_note: WOLF reports Q4 FY26 (June quarter) against guidance of $140-160M revenue, negative non-GAAP gross margin and flat opex. Three things decide the print and the reaction. First, revenue mix: AI datacenter grew ~30% QoQ in Q3 off a small base; another leg up plus 200mm power-device qualifications at Mohawk Valley should offset still-soft auto and volatile materials orders, landing revenue near $152M. Second, the margin trajectory: underutilization at Siler City and Durham keeps GAAP gross margin near -24%, but investors want evidence of sequential improvement toward the company's path to breakeven. Third, cash burn: with the refinancing cutting annualized cash interest ~65% to ~$145M and net capex minimal (~$5M in Q3 after subsidies), the swing factor is the timing of AMIC/ITC refunds and NY grants in investing flows. Watch FY27 guidance: a revenue range above ~$150-170M with a commitment to improving gross margin and a credible update on the long-term model (promised by 1H FY27) is the bull case; a guide below $150M or a quarter-end cash-plus-STI print under ~$950M reopens the dilution debate.
validated.reasoning: Anchors: Q3 FY26 actuals (8-K EX-99.1, accession 0000895419-26-000024) — revenue $150.2M, gross loss -$40.0M, GAAP net loss -$119.9M, CFO -$83.8M, cash $695.1M / cash+STI $1,164.8M, total assets $3,147.3M, equity $1,021.7M; Q4 guidance revenue $140-160M, opex ~flat, gross margin negative. My Q4 FY26 estimate: revenue $152M (slightly above midpoint on AI datacenter momentum and 200mm ramp, offset by weak auto/materials), GAAP gross loss -$36M (modest sequential improvement on higher loading but persistent underutilization per 10-Q b0000498), opex $73M (~flat per guidance), interest expense $44M reflecting full-quarter benefit of the March refinancing ($62M annualized savings; ~$145M annualized cash interest post-refi plus PIK/discount amortization), net loss -$143M, non-GAAP net loss -$119M after adding back SBC, restructuring, transformation costs and debt-cost amortization per the company's own non-GAAP definitions. Cash flow: CFO -$79M (lower cash interest offsetting operating losses), gross capex -$30M (management: capex decreasing significantly, increasing earnings without significant additional CapEx), +$35M other investing (ITC/NY incentive reimbursements and ST-investment rotation), net change -$77M, ending cash $618.1M. FY27 path: revenue recovers ~$165→$212M quarterly as AI datacenter scales, 800V auto architectures adopt SiC and materials orders normalize; gross margin grinds from -18% to ~breakeven by Q4 FY27 as underutilization is absorbed; CFO burn narrows from -$70M to -$42M per quarter. FY0 figures combine Predecessor Q1 (incl. +$420.2M reorganization gain) and Successor periods plus my Q4 print; FY26 net income is approximately breakeven solely because of the fresh-start/reorganization gain. FY28 turns gross-margin positive (~8%) on ~$1.05B revenue; FY29 reaches ~$1.4B revenue and operating breakeven approach, with an equity/capital raise embedded in FY29 financing to fund re-investment. Key risks to the downside: EV demand softness, materials pricing, tariff/trade friction, and the timing of government incentive receipts.
